Disclose

/dis-KLOHZ/ - rhymes with suppose · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Disclose means to make known or reveal.

The consent form requires researchers to disclose every known risk before a volunteer signs.

Worked Example

When hackers copied thousands of customer records, the company sat on the news for five weeks before disclosing the breach—long past the seventy-two hours the law allows—and customers learned their passwords had been for sale all along.

Disclose beats 'tell' or 'announce' here because it carries a sense of duty: what is disclosed was private, someone was owed the truth, and the making-known is formal and on the record.

How Disclose Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

reveal

reveal: the general word for uncovering anything hidden, big or small

confide

confide: to share something private with a person you trust

confess

confess: to admit something embarrassing or wrong about yourself

Antonyms

hide

hide: to keep from being seen or known—the plain opposite

mask

mask: to cover something so it passes unnoticed

How Strong Is It? — mention → disclose → proclaim

mention vs. disclose

mention vs. disclose: To mention a fact is to let it drop casually in passing; to disclose it is to put it formally on the record.

proclaim vs. disclose

proclaim vs. disclose: Proclaim outstrips disclose: a company discloses its finances in a filing few will read, while a town crier proclaims news so that no one can possibly miss it.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — dis-

Prefix — dis-: apart, undo

Root — close

Root — close: to shut

Put it together

Put it together: Dis- (undo) + close (shut) = to un-shut. Latin claudere, 'to close,' hides inside: what was closed away—records, risks, names—gets opened. Disclose keeps that door-swinging image alive: the information was shut up somewhere, and disclosing it means lifting the lid for others to see.

Use the root in a new word: enclose

Use the root in a new word: enclose: Please enclose a stamped envelope with your entry form.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal

Disclose lives in laws, contracts, and news reports: it means making known something private, usually because a rule or duty demands it. Its mirror-opposite in this unit is conceal. For everyday sharing, tell or reveal is lighter; save disclose for facts that are owed to someone.
